name: FORCE 2020
holds: Well logs from the Norwegian continental shelf with interpreted lithology, released for a machine-learning competition.
grain: depth sample, one file per well
about: The FORCE 2020 machine-learning competition asked entrants to predict lithology from wireline logs. Its corpus is a set of wells from the Norwegian North Sea, each sampled about every 15 cm down the hole, with an interpreted lithology label on every sample. PetroDB publishes it as one Parquet file per well, so reading one well fetches one file.

Columns keep the source log mnemonics: GR is gamma ray, RHOB bulk density, NPHI neutron porosity, RDEP deep resistivity. The lithology is an integer code in FORCE_2020_LITHOFACIES_LITHOLOGY; the schema document names every class. The dataset column keeps the competition's train and test split. Quote "GROUP" in SQL: it is a reserved word.

queries.title: One well's logs
queries.why: Each well is its own file, named after the well with / written as -. Reading one well is one request, with no file list needed.
queries.sql:
SELECT DEPTH_MD, GR, RHOB, NPHI, RDEP,
       FORCE_2020_LITHOFACIES_LITHOLOGY AS lithology
FROM '{base}/force_2020/wells/15-9-13.parquet'
ORDER BY DEPTH_MD;

queries.title: Several wells at once
queries.why: The well files cannot be listed over HTTP, so wells/_files.json lists them. Read it, keep the wells you want, and pass the addresses to DuckDB. Here: the four wells in block 15/9, compared by lithology.
queries.sql:
SET VARIABLE wells = (
    SELECT list('{base}/force_2020/wells/' || path)
    FROM read_json('{base}/force_2020/wells/_files.json') AS manifest(path)
    WHERE path LIKE '15-9-%'   -- block 15/9
);

SELECT WELL,
       FORCE_2020_LITHOFACIES_LITHOLOGY AS lithology,
       count(*) AS samples,
       round(avg(GR), 1) AS mean_gr
FROM read_parquet(getvariable('wells'))
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY WELL, samples DESC;
queries.python:
import json, urllib.request
import duckdb

base = "{base}/force_2020/wells/"
files = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(base + "_files.json"))
urls = [base + path for path in files if path.startswith("15-9-")]   # block 15/9

mix = duckdb.sql("""
    SELECT WELL,
           FORCE_2020_LITHOFACIES_LITHOLOGY AS lithology,
           count(*) AS samples,
           round(avg(GR), 1) AS mean_gr
    FROM read_parquet($urls)
    GROUP BY ALL
    ORDER BY WELL, samples DESC
""", params={"urls": urls}).df()
queries.polars:
import json, urllib.request
import polars as pl

base = "{base}/force_2020/wells/"
files = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(base + "_files.json"))
urls = [base + path for path in files if path.startswith("15-9-")]   # block 15/9

mix = (
    pl.scan_parquet(urls)
    .group_by("WELL", pl.col("FORCE_2020_LITHOFACIES_LITHOLOGY").alias("lithology"))
    .agg(pl.len().alias("samples"), pl.col("GR").mean().round(1).alias("mean_gr"))
    .sort("WELL", "samples", descending=[False, True])
    .collect()
)

source.text: Data from the FORCE 2020 Machine Predicted Lithology competition. The competition's files and code are in its GitHub repository; the dataset itself is deposited on Zenodo as FORCE 2020 Well well log and lithofacies dataset for machine learning competition. Cite that record when you use it.
